title: Level design/Map creation
author: dreamswedontshare
selftext:
I've been having some fun with creating a 3D fantasy survivor/extraction hybrid for a while. Bought assets for it, so no generation, LLMs only do the coding part.

I was wondering if there was an effective way to make the AI create maps with existing assets that look nice and cohesive. It feels like Astra has a general idea, but the result is often repetitive and too symmetrical despite my prompts, and it also fails at creatinf aesthetically pleasing mountain ranges for example. Haven't tried Opus 5.5 yet.

What's your go-to when designing beautiful maps with Unity Store assets? Do I just suck it up and create them manually?

comments.author: BradSainty
comments.body: I personally think this is the biggest hurdle with AI at the moment, so also interested to hear ideas.

comments.author: M4xs0n
comments.body: You can use reference Images but I doubt it will be as good as it could be (and not cheap). My best bet is designing a skill for it to save as much as possible

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: i haven't used astra but with opus it gets "lazy" it can make levels with help but lots of time its with minimal prompts. Work out what you want. create a simple description, have an ai decompose it into assets, if those are multi part assets have it break those down get to the smallest component you need. Then make sure you come with space rules and others so you can tell the llm what you want. astra has better spatial awareness from what I've read, but with work opus can do ok, I don't even use fable anymore as opus works the same or better for me

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body: I'm not 100% on how unity works compared to something like unreal but for terrain generation you can you can grab real surface height data from maps to create terrain geometry. That is something the model can pull from any number of places on the web, turn into an OBJ or glb and import into your game. From there you can tweak terrain roads etc and ask your model to use the MCP tools available to populate the scene, create layered terrain textures, foliage etc.

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body:
There is no ready to go solution. You can adapt an editor like quake or Wolfenstein but it's not great. 
How about you build a level editor with mcp support and make it open source??

comments.author: gravesisme
comments.body: I usually take a picture of a sketch I make and I also have it build a level editor so I can tweak things

comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body:
I used to create Quake 3 maps in the early 2000s 

Level design is an artform that requires a lot of thought and actual playtesting to optimize it for the human experience. 

AI is going to suck at this. It can give you something that looks plausible on the surface but it can't examine each part of the map and level and carefully evaluate the human experience for each section because it doesn't have human experience.   
  
The way AI will be used professionally and large studios will be use to to generate assets, human will tweak, correct and embellish initial Ai generated assets but the level design is going to be human.

replies.author: Sencha-Games
replies.body: Respect to Quake mappers! What do you think of [my level editor](https://packaged-media.redd.it/magyji8h75rh1/pb/m2-res_480p.mp4?m=DASHPlaylist.mpd&var=sgpssan&v=1&e=1790449200&s=e117bc56f53518045af52a413e62f7bebd6a216c)?

replies.author: Jolly-Rip5973
replies.body:
That looks pretty dope.   
  
I was the using the office map editor that the Quake 3 made for inhouse use to make the game. it wasn't nearly that friendly. I could take me weeks to make a single map.

comments.author: Sencha-Games
comments.body:
Vibe code a level editor!

You can make it in the Hammer/Probuilder lineage, but there are other less explored ways you can make it fun. Like, what if the level editor looked and played like Construction Mode from The Sims?

replies.author: dreamswedontshare
replies.body: That's exactly what I'm doing right now. I'm vibecoding an editor for heightmaps and terrain textures, since I have Prefab World Builder for the rest and that is working really well

comments.author: Significant-Neck-520
comments.body: Considering how much better Opus 5.5 got at creating assets, I think it could work well for level design, but it could still be below par to a skilled human. It can create compositions, but I'm not sure if entering the creativity level we would say the level is interesting.
